subject: Re: Follow-up: third-party subprocessors & data residency (FinSecure)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 17:22:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: third-party subprocessors & data residency (FinSecure)

Hi Sophie / Anna thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and agreed next steps so we all have the same picture: 

Summary of what we covered:
- Primary concern: PII handling for user-generated prompts and embeddings used in search/reranking.
- Data residency: FinSecure requires production data to remain in us-east-1; dev/test can be multi-region.
- Logging & observability: need audit logs for request/response metadata + access logs for at least 90 days.
- Third parties: you asked about telemetry vendors, cloud providers, and any marketplace flows / integrations that might surface metadata to partners.

Immediate next steps (owners):
1) I will send our current SOC 2 summary and our latest subprocessor inventory (Marissa) attached.
2) Rishi will follow up with a short DPA and propose contractual language for data residency and logging retention (Rishi).
3) Sophie / Anna: confirm whether hashed/pseudonymized telemetry is acceptable for your telemetry vendor and confirm any additional evidence your security team needs.

Key notes from our side: 
- Our hosted API stores request logs (request metadata, timestamps, model used, token counts). Customer content (prompt + output) is retained by default for 30 days for debugging/quality; we provide an opt-out and configurable retention policy down to 0 days for enterprise plans.
- We use a small set of subprocessors: cloud providers (AWS us-east-1 primary), monitoring/telemetry (TelemetryLab), analytics (Lookout Analytics for aggregated metrics). The attached CSV lists vendor, purpose, data categories, and subprocessors' region.
- TelemetryLab receives only anonymized/hashed event keys by default; customer content is never sent. We can provide a POP (point of processing) confirmation showing TelemetryLab processing in us-east-1 as well.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_Report_2026Q3.pdf, Redwood_Subprocessors_2026Q3.csv

Happy to jump on a follow-up with your security team next week propose Tue 12/1 or Wed 12/2. Let me know what works.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Follow-up: third-party subprocessors & data residency (FinSecure)

Marissa thanks for the concise recap. A few clarifying questions before we loop in our security/compliance team: 

1) Can you confirm the default retention windows and whether they are configurable per project/account? You mentioned 30 days default and enterprise down to 0 is that available for hosted customers under a contract?
2) For TelemetryLab: what exact event categories are sent (e.g., request metadata only vs. any user-supplied text)? Are event keys salted/hashed on our side before sending?
3) Subprocessors CSV: could you call out which subprocessors have access to plaintext request/response bodies (if any)? Our data policy disallows third-party plaintext access to PII by default.

We are generally fine with telemetry if it’s hashed/anonymized and TelemetryLab operates in us-east-1. Also we need a written confirmation that logs/audit trails for administrative access will be retained for at least 90 days and that you can provide access logs for a compliance audit.

If you can share the SOC2 and subprocessor inventory (received thanks), we’ll set up a security intake next week. Tue 12/1 11am ET works for us.

 Sophie
Head of Security Operations | FinSecure
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sophie Barnes <sophie.barnes@finsecure.com>, Anna Li <anna.li@finsecure.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: third-party subprocessors & data residency (FinSecure)

Thanks Sophie answers inline below and added a few links/attachments: 

1) Retention windows: our hosted plan defaults to 30 days for customer content; enterprise customers can contractually set retention via the Console or DPA to 0/7/30/90 days. We enforce this at the storage layer and can provide attestation in the DPA. (Attachment: Redwood_DPA_template_v2.docx)

2) TelemetryLab: we send only operational telemetry request_id, timestamp, model_id, token_counts, and hashed event_key. No plaintext prompts or outputs are sent. The hashing is performed server-side with a per-customer salt; we can provide the hashing algorithm summary under NDA. TelemetryLab processes telemetry in us-east-1 for accounts with the us region tag.

3) Subprocessors with access to plaintext: only our cloud provider (AWS) may have access at the infrastructure layer; operationally, Redwood engineers do not access customer plaintext except under explicit support requests and with customer audit logs. The attached CSV lists "access_level" per vendor  — filter column Access=plaintext to see the highlights.

Audit logs & admin access: we retain admin/audit logs for 365 days by default; request/response debug logs follow the retention policy above. We can provide access logs for a defined audit window via a signed request and provide a timestamped export (per the DPA).

Links: Subprocessor folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cD_example_subprocessors
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567890

I’ll attach the SOC2 report and the subprocessor CSV to this thread please let me know if you want me to redact any vendor-specific contact info before sharing with your broader team.

Marissa

We can include the following in the DPA/contract language: 
- Contractual data residency clause (primary processing in us-east-1)
- Retention guarantees for request/response content; ability to set to 0 days for sensitive accounts
- Admin/audit log retention (365 days) and mechanisms for export for audits
- Representation that telemetry vendors receive only hashed/salted keys and no plaintext content

I’ve started a DPA draft and uploaded it (Redwood_DPA_template_v2.docx) to the folder Marissa linked. If FinSecure legal wants edits, we can accept tracked changes or propose a short redline call.
